title: fix(fields): the editable date-time faces refuse an impossible stored day instead of rolling it (objectui#10474)
body:
Fixes #10474
Clause-②: no

## What changed

`packages/fields/src/widgets/nativeDateValue.ts` gets a new predicate, `isImpossibleStoredDay`. It reads the stored value's leading `YYYY-MM-DD` as written and asks the read faces' shared check (`isRealCalendarDate` from `@object-ui/core`, objectui#10026 / objectui#10301). It runs before any `new Date(...)`, for every spelling: `Z`, offset, zone-less and date-only.

- `toDateTimeInputValue` returns an empty string for an impossible day. It no longer returns the rolled day (`2026-02-30T10:00:00Z` used to become `2026-03-02T10:00`).
- `fromDateTimeInputValue` returns an impossible-day string unchanged, the same way it already treats an unparseable string. It never re-emits one as the rolled ISO instant.
- The editable `DateTimeField` and the sub-grid's editable `datetime` cell leave the control empty and set `aria-invalid`. They show a notice that names the stored string, and the control's `aria-describedby` points at it. The notice text is `The stored value "VALUE" is not a real date. Pick a date and time to replace it.` Nothing is written until the user picks a new value, because the control only emits on a user edit. When the day is real, the widget's markup is exactly what it was before.
- New i18n key `fields.dateTime.impossibleDay` in all ten packs, plus `FIELD_DEFAULTS` for rendering without a provider. No existing key fitted: the read faces show `—` or the raw string and have no label of their own.
- The `de` quote-pairing ratchet goes from 63 to 64. The new German value adds one matched `„…“` span.

## Measurement: what a `datetime-local` control can show (the triage fork)

I used Chromium 141.0.7390.37 through playwright-core 1.62.1 with `executablePath` set to `/opt/pw-browsers/chromium`, setting `input.value` directly.

| value set | `input.value` read back |
|:--|:--|
| `2026-02-28T10:00` | `2026-02-28T10:00` |
| `2026-02-30T10:00` (zone-less) | empty |
| `2026-02-30T10:00:00Z` | empty |
| `date` control, `2026-02-30` | empty |

`setCustomValidity` does register on the control (`validity.customError` is true).

So the control cannot show the stored string. It sanitises it to empty, including the zone-less spelling that the old adapter passed straight through, which was a silent blank. The ruling allows showing the stored string with an invalid marker, and that is possible beside the control. So this is not the `needs_decision` fork. I followed hypothesis 2 of the dispatch: the control stays empty and a visible, described notice names the stored string. That matches the grid read face's precedent for an unparsable value, which is to show what is actually stored (objectui#3569).

## Pins (`DateTimeField.impossibleDay-10474.test.tsx`)

- Adapter: six impossible spellings (`Z`, `.000Z`, `+08:00`, zone-less, date-only, and `-05:00` on 29 February 2025) are all judged impossible and reach the control as an empty string. `fromDateTimeInputValue` never emits a rolled day.
- `DateTimeField` through a real render, for each spelling: the control value is empty, `aria-invalid="true"`, and the notice names the stored string and is referenced by `aria-describedby`. No rolled day appears anywhere, and a blur with no edit calls `onChange` zero times. A host's own `aria-describedby` is kept next to the notice id. An explicit pick writes the picked instant.
- The sub-grid's editable `datetime` cell gets the same checks: empty control, invalid marker, notice, no write when untouched, and an explicit pick writes the new instant.
- Controls: a real ISO instant round-trips to the same instant and shows no notice. A zone-less value keeps today's truncation. A real day written with an offset (`2026-02-28T23:30:00-05:00`) is kept. `toDateInputValue` still keeps the leading `YYYY-MM-DD` verbatim.

I ran the suite in `TZ=UTC` and `TZ=America/Los_Angeles`: 32 passed in each, including `nativeDateValue.test.ts`.

**Reverse verification**, with the fix committed first: `ablation-replace.mjs` turned the judgement into `return false` (anchor hits went from 1 to 0 and the replacement landed once). That makes the guards dead code, so the adapter behaves exactly as it did before this change. Result: **16 failed, 6 passed**. The 6 that stayed green are the controls and the two explicit-pick cases, as predicted. The restore was checked by blob: the file's blob equals HEAD's and `git diff HEAD` is empty.

## Gates (at head `e58e47294`)

- `vitest run packages/fields/ packages/i18n/`: fields fully green. The first run found 2 red, both in the `de` quote ratchet (63 vs 64). After bumping it, `packages/i18n/` gave 71 files and 1178 tests passed.
- `type-check` for `@object-ui/fields` and `@object-ui/i18n`, run after building the fields dependency closure: exit 0 for both. `--listFiles` shows the new test file is covered.
- ESLint (`--no-inline-config`) on the 19 touched and scoped files: 0 errors. None of the warnings are new in kind. The config does not enable type-aware linting, so this diff cannot change the verdict on any untouched file.
- These all exited 0: `check:i18n-drift`, `check:i18n-keys`, `check:i18n-dead-keys`, `check:control-bytes`, `check:new-line-citations`, changeset presence / fixed / no-major / claims / overwrite, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check-test-path-roots`, `check:self-import` and `check:phantom-deps`.
- NOT MEASURED: `check-eager-locale-catalogues` returned PREREQUISITE NOT MET because it needs a built console bundle. I left that for CI.

## Acceptance notes

- A free-text value that isn't a date (`not a date`) still shows an empty control, as the existing `maps empty and unparseable input to an empty control` test pins. That is outside this card, and nothing here changes it.
- The readonly `DateTimeField` still shows `—` for an impossible day, which is the objectui#10026 ruling's face. Only the editable faces name the stored string.
- Finding, not fixed here: the `date` editor (`toDateInputValue` into `input type=date`, used by `DateField` and the grid `date` cell) keeps `2026-02-30` verbatim, as the card says, but the measurement above shows that Chromium's `date` control sanitises it to empty. So the date-only editor blanks an impossible day silently instead of showing it as written. The dispatch said not to change `toDateInputValue` unless it rolls, and it does not roll, so I reported it for the seat to file.

Implemented by `session_01D486C1axmXnrkJMNUfz2eb` (seat `domain:ui#3`).
